msgs.title: The same rule can pay you one year and wreck you the next.
msgs.pub:
The same rule can pay you one year and wreck you the next.

What works in a bull market fails in a bear market, and the reverse holds too.

Before you pick a stock, name the market you are in.

Trend up or trend down. Your rules come after that call.

Get the regime right first, and the ticker matters far less.

msgs.fr:
Rules that win in one market regime lose in the other, so the first job is to identify the regime before picking anything.
A rerun of one of your best notes, rewritten.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: Waiting for breakeven is the costliest plan in most portfolios.
msgs.pub:
Waiting for breakeven is the costliest plan in most portfolios.

"I'll get out when I'm back to even."

That one line turns a three-week mistake into a three-year hostage situation.

The stock has no idea where you bought it.

It owes you nothing, least of all a trip back.

Your entry price is a memory, so judge the position at today's price.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: The investor who survives a panic usually wrote the plan before it.
msgs.pub:
The investor who survives a panic usually wrote the plan before it.

Marcus Aurelius ran an empire through war and plague.

At night, in camp, he wrote notes to himself that were never meant for anyone else.

He used them to steady his mind before the next day's decisions.

In a panic, retail reads headlines all night and writes nothing down.

So fear makes the plan on the spot.

I keep a short note for each position, with why I own it and the price where that reason dies.

When the screen goes red, I read the note before the chart.

Write yours on a calm day.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: The most expensive thing in a late bull market is certainty.
msgs.pub:
The most expensive thing in a late bull market is certainty.

Montaigne had a medal struck with a pair of scales held level.

His motto on it admitted how little he knew.

He spent the rest of his life writing about his own doubts, and his book still sells.

Today the perma-bulls and the doom accounts both speak with full conviction.

Certainty gets the clicks, so both sides keep selling it.

I keep my view, and I keep a line in the sand where I am wrong.

That level is my medal.

Size every position so being wrong costs you little.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: Your next big drawdown will hurt less if you live through it today, on paper.
msgs.pub:
Your next big drawdown will hurt less if you live through it today, on paper.

Seneca was one of the richest men in Rome.

He still told a friend to set aside a few days to live on cheap food and rough clothes.

He wanted to meet the thing he feared before it arrived.

Most investors meet their drawdown for the first time when it is already in the account.

The pain is new, so they sell near the low.

I can be wrong about when the next one comes. I am sure it comes.

This week, open your portfolio and cut every line by a third in your head.

If you can sit with that number, you can hold through it.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: The calmest investor in a crash owns shares with no loan on them.
msgs.pub:
The calmest investor in a crash owns shares with no loan on them.

Margin turns a drawdown into a deadline.

Nobody can call a margin on a share you own outright.

Picture someone who bought near the lows, paid cash, and stopped checking the quote.

The bear market passed over their head.

The trader next to them on borrowed money was right on direction and still got shaken out at the bottom.

Low prices and no debt make a quiet edge, and few people have the patience to use it.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: Every sharp drop runs into someone who was waiting for it.
msgs.pub:
Every sharp drop runs into someone who was waiting for it.

Retail on margin and options buyers sell because the screen turned red.

Under them sit patient bids, placed weeks ago at prices chosen on a quiet day.

The panic pushes into those orders and slowly runs out of fuel.

That is why most flushes stop sooner than they feel like they will.

I want to be the one whose order is already sitting there.

Pick your price when nothing is happening, and let the loud day come to you.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: In a real selloff, your best stock drops with your worst one.
msgs.pub:
In a real selloff, your best stock drops with your worst one.

Funds need cash, and quality is the easiest thing to sell.

Picture someone who owns a solid company that pays its dividend on time.

The price slides for a month and they start to doubt the business.

The business is the same. The quote moved.

If you own it outright, you can let the quote do what it wants.

The ones who suffer are the holders on margin, because the drop picks their exit for them.
